The Emco Emcoturn E25 is a compact bar-and-chuck lathe built around a 25.5 mm (1.0 in) bar passage, a 85 mm (3.3 in) maximum turning diameter and a main spindle that runs to 6,300 rpm. It is the smallest of the three Emcoturn E machines, and everything about it is scaled to small parts: 100 mm (3.9 in) of X travel, 300 mm (11.8 in) of Z and 405 mm (15.9 in) between centres.

The Emco Emcoturn E45 is a universal turning centre for bar up to 45 (51) mm and chuck parts within a 220/300 mm turning diameter. What sets it apart inside the Emcoturn E range is how many ways it can be configured. Emco lists a plain version for stationary tools with tailstock, an MY version with driven tools, C axis and Y axis, and SM and SMY versions that swap the tailstock for a counter spindle.

With 22 kW (29.5 hp) and 305 Nm (225.0 lb-ft) at the main spindle, the Emco Emcoturn E65 is the heavy end of the Emcoturn E range: a universal turning centre for bar listed as ø 65 (95) mm and chuck parts up to 500 mm (19.7 in) in diameter. The torque figure is what separates it from its smaller siblings. It allows real roughing in steel at diameters where the smaller machines would be finishing.

Small parts finished on both ends in one cycle: that is the job of the Emco Maxxturn 25. It pairs an 8,000 rpm main spindle with a counter spindle of the same speed, passes 25.4 mm (1.0 in) bar and turns up to 114 mm (4.5 in) in diameter, all inside a machine that weighs 2,100 kg (4,630 lb).

The Emco Maxxturn 45 G2 gives its counter spindle the same rating as its main spindle: 15 kW (20.1 hp) and 100 Nm (73.8 lb-ft) at each end, both listed as 0-7000 rpm. For a bar lathe with a passage of Ø 45 (51) mm, that symmetry is the point. The second operation can cut as hard as the first, so the work can be split evenly between the two sides and neither spindle waits on the other.

Turret Stations: 12 (VDI30, optionally VDI40, or 12-station BMT55, or 16-station BMT45)

Description: The Emco Maxxturn 95 is a shaft lathe. It has 1,430 mm (56.3 in) between centres, 1,360 mm (53.5 in) of Z travel, an automatic tailstock and a spindle that passes 95 mm (3.7 in) bar, and Emco lists a steady rest for it. There is no counter spindle in the table: the machine is built to turn long parts between a chuck and a centre.

Three bed lengths define the Emco Maxxturn 110. Z travel is listed as 1560-2560-3560 mm and tailstock travel as 1300/2300/3300 mm, and Emco describes the range as a main spindle with three bed lengths up to 3500 mm. Around that sits a large-capacity lathe: 680 mm (26.8 in) maximum turning diameter, 840 mm (33.1 in) swing over the bed and a 110 mm (4.3 in) spindle bore that passes 95 mm (3.7 in) bar.

The Emco Maxxturn 200 turns parts up to 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in diameter and, on the longest bed, 2200 / 4200 / 6200 mm between centres. Emco gives a maximum workpiece weight of 6 t. This is heavy-duty turning for rolls, shafts and large hollow parts, with a main spindle rated 84 kW (112.6 hp) and 6,410 Nm (4728.0 lb-ft).

The Emco S45 is a two-axis CNC lathe with a short bed: 310 mm (12.2 in) of Z travel, 160 mm (6.3 in) of X and a 45 mm (1.8 in) bar passage. Emco sells it as a plain production lathe, and the table reflects that. There is one spindle, one 12-station turret, and no Y travel or counter spindle row.

Torque is the headline of the Emco S65: 192 Nm (141.6 lb-ft) from an 18 kW (24.1 hp) main spindle that tops out at 4,200 rpm. It is a two-axis CNC lathe for 65 mm (2.6 in) bar and chuck parts up to 310 mm (12.2 in) in diameter, and the low top speed tells you where it is meant to work, on larger diameters and tougher cuts than a small bar lathe sees.

The Emco Universalturn 50 is sold in three versions, and the drive train changes with them. The M and MY machines have a belt-driven main spindle with VDI 30 (M+MY) tooling. The SMY machine has direct-drive spindles at both ends and a BMT45P turret. The torque row says as much: 197 Nm (belt drive M+MY) / 146 Nm (direct drive SMY). All versions run to 6,200 rpm on a DIN 55026 KK5 nose and pass bar listed as 50 / 50.8 mm through a 59 mm (2.3 in) bore.
Spindle Torque: 197 Nm (belt drive M+MY) / 146 Nm (direct drive SMY)

Description: Two bed lengths and an optional counter spindle are what the Emco Universalturn 90 adds to the shaft-lathe layout of the Maxxturn 95 . Distance between centres is 1430 | 2230 mm and Z travel 1360 | 2160 mm, with bar listed as up to 102 mm and a maximum turning diameter of 500 mm (19.7 in).
This model was not found in Eurotech's current lineup when we checked on 2026-10-03 . It may be a superseded or older model; the specifications below are as we last recorded them.
Rapid Traverse Rate: 30 m/min X; 30 m/min Z; 20 m/min Y

Description: The Feeler FT-200(MC) is the smallest lathe in the FT series, which Feeler heads as horizontal box way lathes. It takes an 8 in (203 mm) chuck, turns up to 300 mm (11.8 in) in diameter and 487 mm (19.2 in) in length, and its spindle reaches 4,500 rpm. The MC in brackets marks the driven-tool version of the same machine.

A metre between chuck and centre defines the Feeler FT-250(MC). Maximum turning length is 1,037 mm (40.8 in) on a 10 in (254 mm) chuck box way lathe, with a turning diameter of 420 mm (16.5 in). That is roughly twice the length of the FT-200(MC ) below it.

The Feeler FT-250SY is the twin-spindle, Y-axis lathe of the FT box way series. The S and Y in the name show up in two rows of the table: a Y axis travel of 100 (±50) mm, and a Z/E travel of 1,050/947 mm, where E is the axis on which a second spindle travels. There is no tailstock entry.

The Feeler FT-350(MC) is a 12 in (305 mm) chuck box way lathe for heavy turning, with a maximum turning diameter of 620 mm (24.4 in) and a turning length of 1,060 mm (41.7 in). Feeler says the FT-350 emphasizes heavy cutting and stability.

Big bore, long bed: the Feeler FT-350AL(MC) is the FT lathe for oilfield-style tube and long heavy shafts. Its spindle has an A2-11 nose with a 131 mm (5.2 in) through-hole, bar capacity is 115 mm (4.5 in), and the maximum turning length is 1,520 mm (59.8 in).

The Feeler FTC-10 is a small two-axis CNC lathe: a 6 in chuck as standard with 8 in in brackets as the alternative, a maximum turning diameter of φ240 mm and a turning length of 255 mm (10.0 in). It is the smallest of the three FTC linear guide lathes.

Feeler prints the FTC-20(L) as one column covering two bed lengths. The standard FTC-20 turns 343 mm between chuck and tailstock; the L version, shown in brackets, turns 613 mm. Z travel follows the same pattern at 380 (650) mm.

The Feeler FTC-30 is the largest FTC linear guide lathe, a 10 in chuck machine with a maximum turning diameter of φ450 mm (φ17.7 in) and a turning length of 621 mm (24.4 in). A 12 in chuck is shown in brackets as the alternative.

The Feeler FTC-300 is the smallest lathe in the FTC/FTB inclined-bed series: a 6 in (152 mm) chuck, ø300 mm (ø11.8 in) of maximum turning diameter and 320 mm (12.6 in) of turning length. Feeler gives its footprint as just 2.5 m × 1.5 m and calls it perfect for small parts.

Three bed lengths share one column in Feeler's table for the FTC-350/L/XL, an 8 in (203 mm) chuck lathe with a ø350 mm (ø13.8 in) maximum turning diameter. Turning length is 340 mm on the standard bed, 660 mm on the L and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) on the XL. Z travel follows at 380, 700 and 1,040 mm.

A Y axis with 80 (±40) mm (3.1 (±1.6) in) of travel is what defines the Feeler FTC-350LY. It is a single-length machine on the 8 in (203 mm) FTC-350 platform, with 585 mm (23.0 in) of turning length and 625 mm (24.6 in) of Z travel.

Feeler's FTC-350MC/LMC/XLMC is the turning-milling version of the 8 in (203 mm) FTC-350, offered on three bed lengths. The figure to read first is the turning diameter: ø235 mm (ø9.3 in). The plain FTC-350/L/XL turns ø350 mm on the same chuck and spindle, so the milling turret takes a good deal of swing away.

Two spindles and no tailstock: the Feeler FTC-350S/LS/XLS is the sub-spindle version of the FTC-350, in three bed lengths. Every spindle row in its column carries two values. Chuck size is 8/6 in (203/152 mm), spindle nose A2-6/A2-5, top speed 4,500/6,000 rpm and bore ø62/ø56 mm, the first for the main spindle and the second for the smaller one facing it.

Sub-spindle and driven tools together are what the Feeler FTC-350SLMC/SXLMC adds to the FTC-350 line. It comes in two lengths, with 510 mm (20.1 in) or 850 mm (33.5 in) of turning length, and its turret is listed as 12-BMT 55.

The Feeler FTC-350SLY carries every option the FTC-350 family offers in one column: a second spindle, and a Y axis with 80 (±40) mm (3.1 (±1.6) in) of travel. It is listed in a single length, with 515 mm (20.3 in) of turning length.

With a 10 in (254 mm) chuck and an A2-8 spindle nose, the Feeler FTC-430/L/XL is the mid-size two-axis lathe of the FTC/FTB series. Maximum turning diameter is ø430 mm (ø16.9 in) and the three bed lengths give 335 mm, 655 mm or 995 mm (39.2 in) of turning length.

Feeler lists the FTC-430LY/XLY as the Y-axis lathe of the 10 in (254 mm) class, with 100 (±50) mm (3.9 (±2.0) in) of Y travel and a 12-BMT 55 turret. It comes in two lengths: 435 mm (17.1 in) or 775 mm (30.5 in) of turning length.

The Feeler FTC-430MC/LMC/XLMC puts a 12-VDI 40 driven-tool turret on the 10 in (254 mm) FTC-430. Unlike the smaller milling lathe in the family, it does so without losing swing: the maximum turning diameter stays at ø430 mm (ø16.9 in), the same as the two-axis FTC-430/L/XL .

Feeler singles out the FTC-450L/(MC) in its series text: a 45-degree high-rigidity bed and 30 m/min feed, with turning-milling as an option. In the table it is a 10 in (254 mm) chuck lathe with a ø450 mm (ø17.7 in) maximum turning diameter and 650 mm (25.6 in) of turning length.

The Feeler FTC-550 is a 12 in (305 mm) chuck lathe that turns up to ø550 mm (ø21.7 in) over a length of 600 mm (23.6 in). Z travel is the same 600 mm. It stands alone in the table: one length, no milling column, no long bed.

Heavy turning is the brief for the Feeler FTC-640(MC). Feeler states that the FTC-640 is equipped with an A2-11 spindle and two-speed gearbox, delivering high torque for heavy cutting on large workpieces, and the table backs that with a 15 in (381 mm) chuck and a top speed of 2,000 rpm marked ZF gear transmission.

The Feeler FTC-640L(MC) is the long bed of the 15 in (381 mm) class, with 1,500 mm (59.1 in) of Z travel. No other lathe in the FTC/FTB table travels as far. The same spindle as the short bed drives it: an A2-11 nose, a ø131 mm (ø5.2 in) bore and 2,000 rpm through a ZF gear transmission.

The Feeler FVT-1000 is a heavy-duty vertical turning lathe with a 32 in (813 mm) chuck and a maximum turning diameter of φ1,000 mm. Turning length, and Z travel, is 850 mm (33.5 in); X travel is 540 mm (21.3 in).

The Feeler HT-30MC is the base model of the HT turn-and-mill series: a 10 in chuck slant-bed lathe with a 12-station servo-driven turret, built for parts that need milling and drilling as well as turning. Maximum turning diameter is φ356 mm (φ14.0 in) and turning length 705 mm (27.8 in).

The Feeler HT-30SY is the two-spindle, Y-axis version of the HT turn-and-mill lathe, the model that can finish both ends of a part without an operator turning it round. Its column in Feeler's table carries paired values where the others have one: spindle speed 3,500/6,000 rpm, spindle nose JIS A2-8/JIS A2-5, bar capacity φ78/φ45 mm. The first of each pair matches the main spindle of the single-spindle models, so the second describes the sub-spindle.

A Y axis on the turret is what the Feeler HT-30Y adds to the HT turn-and-mill lathe. With it the driven tool can move off the spindle centreline, so the machine can mill flat-bottomed keyways to width, cut pockets and hexes, and drill holes that are not on a diameter, all in the same clamping as the turning.

The Fryer ET-16 is the entry model of the Easy Turn toolroom lathes: 16 in (406 mm) of swing over the bed, 40 in (1,016 mm) between centers and a 2.05 in (52 mm) spindle bore on a Camlock D1-6 nose. It is a flat-bed CNC lathe with dual handles, built for a machinist who turns one shaft, cuts one thread or repairs one part at a time.

With 18 in (457 mm) of swing and a two-range headstock, the Fryer ET-18 is the Easy Turn toolroom lathe that most general turning ends up on. It shares its bed, 40 in (1,016 mm) center distance and footprint with the ET-16 , and differs in the headstock and in what can be ordered for it.

Everything else in Fryer's table is common with the ET-30 , so the choice between the two is purely one of diameter.

Description: The Geminis GT5i-G2 is a heavy horizontal CNC lathe with a 1,400 mm (55.1 in) swing over the bed and a 1,050 mm (41.3 in) swing over the carriage. Geminis lists two maximum workpiece weights for it, 8,000 / 12,000 kg (17,637 / 26,455 lb), and a length range of 1 - 24 m (39.4 - 944.9 in).
Chip Evacuation: By means of optional double conveyors
Spindle Speed Ranges: 4 speed ranges with automatic changeover and main shaft oscillation

Description: The Geminis GT5i-G4 is a horizontal CNC lathe with a 1,400 mm (55.1 in) swing over the bed, built on a bed with 4 upper guides Box Type where the GT5i-G2 of the same swing lists 2. That guideway row is the reason to consider this model instead of its sibling.
Chip Evacuation: By means of optional double conveyors
Spindle Speed Ranges: 4 speed ranges with automatic changeover and main shaft oscillation

Description: The Geminis GT7i-G2 is a horizontal CNC lathe sized between the GT5i-G2 and the GT9i-G2 : 1,800 mm (70.9 in) of swing over the bed, 1,400 mm (55.1 in) over the carriage, and workpiece weights listed as 12,000 / 25,000 kg (26,455 / 55,115 lb).
Chip Evacuation: By means of optional double conveyors
Spindle Speed Ranges: 4 speed ranges with automatic changeover and main shaft oscillation

Description: The Geminis GT9i-G2 is a large horizontal CNC lathe whose capacity rows are ranges instead of single values: swing over the bed from 2,000 to 2,600 mm (78.7 to 102.4 in) and swing over the carriage from 1,600 to 2,200 mm (63.0 to 86.6 in). One model name therefore covers several sizes of machine, and the swing has to be fixed when the lathe is ordered.
Chip Evacuation: By means of optional double conveyors
Spindle Speed Ranges: 4 speed ranges with automatic changeover and main shaft oscillation

Description: The Geminis GT11i-G2 is a very large horizontal CNC lathe: 2,600 to 3,600 mm (102.4 to 141.7 in) of swing over the bed, 2,000 to 3,000 mm (78.7 to 118.1 in) over the carriage, and maximum workpiece weights listed as 45,000 / 150,000 kg (99,206 / 330,688 lb).
Chip Evacuation: By means of optional double conveyors
Spindle Speed Ranges: 4 speed ranges with automatic changeover and main shaft oscillation

Description: The Goodway GA-3600/W24 is a single-purpose lathe: it turns aluminum wheels from 13 in to 24 in. Goodway takes its GA box-way platform, fits a 45 kW (60.3 hp) 15 min. spindle motor and a wheel chuck interface, and builds the machine around chip removal and fast loading.

The Goodway GLA-1500 is a small-part production lathe built around its loader: a 6 in chuck machine with Ø200 mm (7.9 in) of turning diameter and 250 mm (9.8 in) of turning length that Goodway equips with a gantry type loading and unloading system and fits into a 2.5 m2 footprint.

The Goodway GLS-150 is a 6 in, 6,000 rpm slant-bed lathe on linear guideways, with 500 mm (19.7 in) of turning length and Ø51 mm (2.0 in) bar capacity. It is the faster of the two machines Goodway sells on this bed. The GLS-200 is the same machine with an 8 in chuck and a larger bore.
An 8 in chuck, Ø65 mm (2.6 in) through the spindle and 4,500 rpm: the Goodway GLS-200 is the larger-bore version of the GLS-150 , built on the same linear-guideway slant bed.

The Goodway GLS-1500 takes a 6 in big-bore, 6,000 rpm linear-guideway lathe and offers it in six variations, from a plain two-axis machine to a Y-axis, sub-spindle turning center, plus a gang-tool version. Bar capacity is Ø51 mm (2.0 in), and the frame occupies about 4.5 m2 by Goodway's figure.

Goodway's GLS-2000 is the 8 in member of the GLS-1500 series: a linear-guideway slant-bed turning center with an 8 in big-bore chuck, Ø65 mm (2.6 in) bar capacity and a 4,500 rpm spindle. Its place in the lineup is easy to state. It is the smallest Goodway lathe that combines a Ø65 mm bore with an optional Y-axis and sub-spindle.

The Goodway GLS-2800 is a Ø75 mm (3.0 in) bar capacity turning center on linear guideways, with a 3,500 rpm spindle and a choice of 720 mm (28.3 in) or 1,220 mm (48.0 in) of turning length. It is the smaller of two models on this bed; the GLS-3300 has the bigger bore and motor.

Ø90 mm (3.5 in) of bar capacity on linear guideways defines the Goodway GLS-3300. Large-bore lathes are more often built on box ways, so this model suits shops that want the bore for big bar and tube but spend most of their time on lighter, faster cuts.

The Goodway GS-200 is an 8 in box-way turning center with Ø65 mm (2.6 in) bar capacity, a 4,500 rpm spindle and Ø420 mm (16.5 in) of turning diameter. Where Goodway's GLS lathes of similar chuck size ride on linear guideways, the GS-200 uses box ways on a 30° slant bed, which the maker ties to heavy-duty and interrupted cuts.

Fit a 10 in chuck and a Ø75 mm (3.0 in) bore to the GS-200 and the result is the Goodway GS-280. Spindle speed drops to 3,500 rpm, and the larger chuck shortens the usable turning length to 534 mm (21.0 in) on the standard bed or 1,134 mm (44.6 in) on the L bed.

The Goodway GS-2000 is the 8 in entry to the GS-2000 / GS-3000 series, Goodway's main line of box-way slant-bed turning centers. It pairs Ø65 mm (2.6 in) bar capacity and a 4,500 rpm spindle with a frame sized for much larger work: Ø570 mm (22.4 in) of turning diameter, 300 mm (11.8 in) of X travel and a Ø700 mm (27.6 in) swing.

A 10 in chuck, Ø75 mm (3.0 in) of bar capacity and 3,500 rpm place the Goodway GS-2800 second in the four-size GS-2000 / GS-3000 series. It uses the smaller of the series' two motors, 15 kW (20.1 hp) continuous and 18.5 kW (24.8 hp) for 30 min., on the common box-way bed.

The Goodway GS-3300 is the 12 in model of the GS-3000 half of the series, and the point where the bigger motor arrives: 18.5 kW (24.8 hp) continuous and 22 kW (29.5 hp) on the 30 min. rating. Goodway shows this 22 kW spindle on the series page as a feature of the GS-3300. Bar capacity is Ø90 mm (3.5 in) and top speed 3,000 rpm.

Top of the GS-2000 / GS-3000 series by bore, the Goodway GS-3600 carries a 15 in chuck and passes Ø105 mm (4.1 in) bar at up to 2,500 rpm. It keeps the 18.5 kW (24.8 hp) continuous, 22 kW (29.5 hp) 30 min. motor of the GS-3300 .

Description: Goodway's GTH-2000 applies the parallel twin-spindle, gantry-loaded layout of the GTH series to 10 in chuck work. It turns Ø300 mm (11.8 in) and 205 mm (8.1 in) long on each of two side-by-side spindles with A2-6 noses.

The Goodway GTS-150 is a twin-spindle, twin-turret turning center for small parts: two opposed 6 in spindles with Ø42 mm (1.7 in) bar capacity running to 6,000 rpm, each served by its own 12-station turret. A part is turned on spindle 1, handed across to spindle 2 and finished on the back while the next part starts.

With 8 in chucks, 11 kW (14.8 hp) continuous on each spindle and a box-way bed, the Goodway GTS-200 is the heavier-cutting size of the GTS twin-spindle, twin-turret family. Bar capacity is Ø51 mm (2.0 in) and each spindle runs to 4,800 rpm.
The Goodway GTS-260 is the largest of the three GTS models, carrying 10 in chucks on both opposed spindles and passing Ø65 mm (2.6 in) bar. Spindle speed is 4,000 rpm.

The Goodway GTW-1500Y combines two tooling systems that are normally found on different machines: a 12-station live tooling turret for the main spindle and an 8-station gang type tooling system for the sub-spindle. Goodway describes it as joining the capabilities of turret type and SWISS type turning centers, and names the medical and automobile industries as its targets.

Description: Goodway names the work for the GV-780 outright: brake discs, brake drums, gears, wheels, hubs and valves. It is a vertical turning center for 15 in and 18 in chucks that turns Ø820 mm (32.3 in) and 660 mm (26.0 in) high, within a footprint the maker puts at approximately 6.3 m2.

The Goodway GV-1000 is a turret-type vertical turning center for chucks from 18 in to 32 in, turning Ø1,000 mm (39.4 in) and 760 mm (29.9 in) high. It sits between Goodway's compact GV-780 and the ram-type GV-1100 : bigger than the first, but still a turret lathe with quick tool changes instead of a ram and tool magazine.

The Goodway GV-1100 is a ram-type vertical turning lathe with a Ø1,100 mm (43.3 in) table, a moving cross rail and a BT50 tool changer. It turns parts up to Ø1,200 mm (47.2 in) in diameter, 1,000 mm (39.4 in) high and 4,000 kg (8,818 lb) in weight, and is the smallest of the four GV-1 models.

Second in the GV-1 range of moving-rail vertical lathes, the Goodway GV-1200 has a Ø1,250 mm (49.2 in) table and turns Ø1,350 mm (53.1 in). It is more than a slightly wider GV-1100 : three figures step up together, and each one changes what work the machine can take.

The Goodway GV-1600 carries 8,000 kg (17,637 lb) on a Ø1,600 mm (63.0 in) table and puts 23,900 Nm (17,629 lb-ft) of torque into the cut. Those two numbers, the highest in the GV-1 series, make it the heavy-work model of the range.

Largest of the GV-1 series, the Goodway GV-2000 has a Ø2,000 mm (78.7 in) table and turns the same Ø2,000 mm, with a swing only slightly greater at Ø2,050 mm (80.7 in). Goodway prints two columns for the model, and the single difference between them is table load: 5,000 kg (11,023 lb) or 8,000 kg (17,637 lb).

The Goodway GVB-3000 is the largest machine Goodway lists: a bridge-type vertical turning center with a Ø3,000 mm (118.1 in) table, Ø3,500 mm (137.8 in) of turning diameter and 20,000 kg (44,092 lb) of table load, with 45,000 kg (99,206 lb) available as an option. Maximum spindle torque is 169,700 Nm (125,171 lb-ft).

The Goodway GVF-1112 is a fixed-beam vertical turning lathe with a 1,100 mm (43.3 in) table. Fixed beam means the cross rail does not move: the ram alone supplies the vertical travel, 900 mm (35.4 in) in Z, and the maximum turning height is 900 mm as well. In exchange for the lost adjustment, Goodway claims the highest structural rigidity and damping for the whole machine.

There are two GVF models with a 1,250 mm (49.2 in) table, and the Goodway GVF-1214 is the lighter of them. It turns 1,400 mm (55.1 in) in diameter but carries only 3,700 kg (8,157 lb), the lowest table load in the GVF series and less even than the smaller GVF-1112 .

The Goodway GVF-1215 marks the point in the fixed-beam GVF series where the heavier drive train begins. Table torque jumps to 17,100 Nm (12,613 lb-ft), the tool magazine grows to 16 positions and the optional tooling spindle to 11 kW (14.8 hp) continuous, all on a 1,250 mm (49.2 in) table.

An 8,000 kg (17,637 lb) table load and 23,900 Nm (17,629 lb-ft) of torque make the Goodway GVF-1618 the heaviest-duty model of the fixed-beam GVF line below the 2,000 mm size. Its table measures 1,600 mm (63.0 in) and it turns 1,800 mm (70.9 in).

The Goodway GVF-2023 turns 2,300 mm (90.6 in) on a 2,000 mm (78.7 in) table. It is the largest fixed-beam GVF, and it turns a wider part than the moving-rail GV-2000 of the same table size, which stops at Ø2,000 mm.

The Goodway GVH-2000 opens the SUPER GV series of very large vertical turning centers. Its Ø2,000 mm (78.7 in) table carries 10,000 kg (22,046 lb), it turns Ø2,300 mm (90.6 in), and its table drive produces 59,700 Nm (44,035 lb-ft). That torque is two and a half times the 23,900 Nm of the GVF-2023 , a machine with the same table diameter.

With a Ø2,500 mm (98.4 in) table rated for 15,000 kg (33,069 lb), the Goodway GVH-2500 is the larger of the two one-piece-column machines in the SUPER GV series. It turns Ø2,800 mm (110.2 in) under a Ø3,000 mm (118.1 in) swing.

The Goodway GVI-350 is an inverted vertical turning center with two 12 in spindles and two turrets, laid out so that a part is machined on both sides and passed from one spindle to the other with no robot in between. Maximum turning diameter is Ø350 mm (13.8 in) and turning height 400 mm (15.7 in).

The HNK HCT-45T is a CNC vertical lathe for crankthrows, the forged webs of built-up crankshafts for large ship engines. Its table is 4,500 mm (177.2 in) in diameter with a maximum swing of 5,000 mm (196.9 in), and it carries 60,000 kg (132,275 lb).
With a 5,000 mm (196.9 in) table and 5,400 mm (212.6 in) of swing, the HNK HCT-50T turns crankthrows for large marine engines up to 70,000 kg (154,321 lb).

The HNK HCT-52T is barely larger in diameter than the size below it, yet its drive is a class larger. This crankthrow vertical lathe has a 5,200 mm (204.7 in) table, 5,600 mm (220.5 in) of swing, a 171 kW (229.3 hp) table motor and a load rating of 90,000 kg (198,413 lb).
The HNK HCT-55T is the largest crankthrow lathe HNK lists: a 5,500 mm (216.5 in) table, 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of swing and 90,000 kg (198,413 lb) on the table.

The HNK NT-10/12F is the smallest CNC vertical turning lathe in the NT series: a 1,000 mm (39.4 in) table, 1,250 mm (49.2 in) of swing and cutting diameter, and a turning height of 800 mm (31.5 in). It is also the fastest. The table runs to about 450 rpm in two speed steps, which no larger NT matches, so small rings and discs can be cut at a sensible surface speed.

The HNK NT-12/16 is where the NT series gets a movable cross rail. On a 1,250 mm (49.2 in) table with 1,600 mm (63.0 in) of swing and cutting diameter, the rail travels vertically in 3 steps of 250 mm (9.8 in), and the maximum turning height rises to 1,300 mm (51.2 in).

Two NT machines share the 1,250 mm (49.2 in) table, and the HNK NT-12/16F is the low one. Its cross rail is fixed, the maximum turning height is 900 mm (35.4 in), and the swing and cutting diameter is 1,600 mm (63.0 in). The NT-12/16 has the same table and swing but a stepped rail and 1,300 mm (51.2 in) of turning height.

The HNK NT-16/20 is the stepped-rail version of the 1,600 mm (63.0 in) table machine, and it is taller than it is wide in proportion: 1,660 mm (65.4 in) of turning height against a 2,000 mm (78.7 in) swing. Among the NT machines with the 200 x 200 mm (7.9 x 7.9 in) ram, this one has the most room under the rail.

A 1,600 mm (63.0 in) table under a fixed cross rail: that is the HNK NT-16/20F. Swing and cutting diameter reach 2,000 mm (78.7 in), but the turning height is 900 mm (35.4 in), the same figure as the smaller NT-12/16F . It is a wide, low machine.

With the HNK NT-20/25 the NT series changes ram. The table is 2,000 mm (78.7 in), the swing and cutting diameter 2,500 mm (98.4 in), and the ram section grows to 240 x 240 mm (9.4 x 9.4 in) from the 200 x 200 mm (7.9 x 7.9 in) of the NT-16/20 below it.

20,000 kg (44,092 lb) is the figure that defines the HNK NT-25/30. This CNC vertical turning lathe has a 2,500 mm (98.4 in) table and 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of swing and cutting diameter, and it carries far more than the 12,000 kg (26,455 lb) of the NT-20/25 one size down.

From the HNK NT-30/40 upward, the NT specification stops being a single machine and becomes a menu. This vertical turning lathe has a 3,000 mm (118.1 in) table and 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of swing and cutting diameter, but the ram head's Z travel is listed as 1,300/1,500/2,000/2,200/2,500 mm (51.2/59.1/78.7/86.6/98.4 in) and the ram section as 300 x 300, 350 x 350 or 400 x 400 mm (11.8 x 11.8, 13.8 x 13.8 or 15.7 x 15.7 in).

The HNK NT-40/50 turns parts up to 5,000 mm (196.9 in) in diameter on a 4,000 mm (157.5 in) table, and its table motor is given as a single figure: A.C 100 kW (134.1 hp). Smaller NT machines list a pair of ratings. This is the first size where one number stands alone in that row.

Tooling is what changes on the HNK NT-50/60. This 5,000 mm (196.9 in) table machine is the first in the NT series to take 60 x 60 mm (2.4 x 2.4 in) tool shanks, where the NT-40/50 and every size below it use 40 x 40 mm (1.6 x 1.6 in). A heavier shank carries a longer overhang and a bigger insert, which is what a 6,000 mm (236.2 in) swing demands.

Table load more than doubles at the HNK NT-60/70. The 6,000 mm (236.2 in) table is rated for 150,000 kg (330,688 lb), where the NT-50/60 beneath it stops at 60,000 kg (132,275 lb). Swing and cutting diameter are 7,000 mm (275.6 in) and the turning height is 3,500 mm (137.8 in).

The HNK NT-80/100 is a 10,000 mm (393.7 in) swing vertical turning lathe with an 8,000 mm (315.0 in) table, and it is the point in the NT series where the table drive becomes a D.C motor: 265 kW (355.4 hp). Every smaller NT is listed with an A.C drive.

At the top of the NT series, the HNK NT-100/160 pairs a 10,000 mm (393.7 in) table with a maximum swing and cutting diameter of 16,000 mm (629.9 in). The gap between those two figures is the widest in the range. The NT-80/100 swings 10,000 mm (393.7 in) over an 8,000 mm (315.0 in) table, a much closer match.

The HNK VTC-10/12F is the entry size of the VTC vertical turning centers: a 1,000 mm (39.4 in) table with a C-axis, plus a live milling spindle in the ram. HNK's point for the series is that an indexing table and a live spindle let the machine mill and tap after turning, so a part is finished in a single setup.

Take the 1,250 mm (49.2 in) table of the VTC-12/16F , put a stepped cross rail over it, and the result is the HNK VTC-12/16. Turning height goes from 900 mm (35.4 in) on the VTC-12/16F to 1,300 mm (51.2 in), with the rail moving 250 mm (9.8 in) x 3 steps. Swing and cutting diameter stay at 1,600 mm (63.0 in).

Three VTC models share a 1,600 mm (63.0 in) swing, and the HNK VTC-12/16F is the fixed-rail one. It has a 1,250 mm (49.2 in) table, a fixed type cross rail and 900 mm (35.4 in) of turning height. The VTC-12/16 has a stepped rail and 1,300 mm (51.2 in); the VTC-12/16R is a separate design with a 1,200 mm (47.2 in) table.

The HNK VTC-12/16R does not follow the pattern of the VTC models around it. Its table is 1,200 mm (47.2 in), not the 1,250 mm (49.2 in) of the VTC-12/16 ; its control is listed as Fanuc 0i-T, with Fanuc 31i in braces; and its cross rail moves 300 mm (11.8 in) x 2steps. HNK's page does not explain the R, but the table describes a lighter, simpler turning center in the 1,600 mm (63.0 in) swing class.

Of the three 2,000 mm (78.7 in) swing turning centers HNK lists, the VTC-16/20 has the most height: 1,660 mm (65.4 in) under a cross rail that moves 250 mm (9.8 in) x 3 steps. It keeps the 10,000 kg (22,046 lb) table load of the fixed-rail VTC-16/20F and the full control choice of Fanuc 31i-B or Siemens 840D.

The HNK VTC-16/20F is the widest fixed-rail turning center HNK lists: 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of swing and cutting diameter over a 1,600 mm (63.0 in) table, under a rail that does not move. Turning height is 900 mm (35.4 in).

Like its smaller R sibling, the HNK VTC-16/20R is the Fanuc 0i-T machine in its size class. It has a 1,600 mm (63.0 in) table and 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of swing, the same as the VTC-16/20 , but the control row reads Fanuc 0i-T with Fanuc 31i in braces, and Siemens 840D is absent.

The HNK VTC-20/25 is a vertical turning center with a 2,000 mm (78.7 in) table and 2,500 mm (98.4 in) of swing, and it is where the VTC milling spindle gets its first power increase: A.C 18.5/22 kW (24.8/29.5 hp), cont/30min. The VTC-16/20 below it has A.C 15/18.5 kW (20.1/24.8 hp), and the smaller sizes no more than that.

On the HNK VTC-25/30 a 20,000 kg (44,092 lb) part can be turned, milled and drilled without leaving the table. The machine has a 2,500 mm (98.4 in) table, 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of swing and cutting diameter and 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of turning height.

A 4,000 mm (157.5 in) swing, a 30,000 kg (66,138 lb) table and a milling spindle built for torque over speed: the HNK VTC-30/40 marks the change from mid-size to large in the VTC series. Its table is 3,000 mm (118.1 in) across.

There is a wide gap between the two motors on the HNK VTC-40/50. The table drive is A.C 100 kW (134.1 hp). The milling spindle motor is A.C 22/26 kW (29.5/34.9 hp), cont/30min. That ratio says what the machine is: a heavy vertical lathe first, with milling as the finishing capability that saves a second setup.

The HNK VTC-50/60 has a 5,000 mm (196.9 in) table and a 6,000 mm (236.2 in) swing, and its turning tools move up to 60 x 60 mm (2.4 x 2.4 in) shanks. The milling side, by contrast, is carried over unchanged from the VTC-30/40 : ISO 50, about 2,000 rpm, A.C 22/26 kW (29.5/34.9 hp) on a cont/30min basis.

Milling power steps up sharply on the HNK VTC-60/70. The milling spindle motor is A.C 37/45 kW (49.6/60.3 hp), cont/30min, where the VTC-50/60 has A.C 22/26 kW (29.5/34.9 hp). Spindle speed comes down to about 1,500 rpm, and the taper stays ISO 50.

The HNK VTC-80/100 puts the most powerful milling spindle of the VTC series over an 8,000 mm (315.0 in) table. The milling motor is A.C 45/55 kW (60.3/73.8 hp), cont/30min, at up to about 1,500 rpm with an ISO 50 taper. Only the VTC-100/160 matches it.

The largest machine HNK lists in either vertical lathe series is the VTC-100/160: 16,000 mm (629.9 in) of swing and cutting diameter over a 10,000 mm (393.7 in) table, with a live milling spindle and a C-axis. Table load is 450,000 kg (992,063 lb).

The Honor Seiki VL-46A/AR is the smallest vertical lathe in the maker's High Speed Series: a 305 mm (12 in) chuck machine that swings and turns 560 mm (22 in), takes work up to 450 mm (17.7 in) tall and runs its spindle from 25 to 2,500 rpm. Honor Seiki lists the A and the AR in a single column, so one set of figures covers both.

The Honor Seiki VL-46AT is a twin vertical lathe: two spindles and two turrets in one machine, each side with a 305 mm (12 in) chuck, a 560 mm (22 in) swing and turning diameter and a 25-2,500 rpm spindle. Tool positions are listed as 12+12.

Five tool positions, not twelve: that is the figure that defines the Honor Seiki VL-46G. It shares the 305 mm (12 in) chuck, the 25-2,500 rpm spindle and the 450 kg (992 lb) workpiece limit of the other VL-46 models, and it turns the same 560 mm (22 in) diameter at up to 450 mm (17.7 in) of height. Swing is a little larger at 600 mm (23.6 in).

The Honor Seiki VL-46H has the largest swing and the smallest turning diameter of the four VL-46 columns. It clears 650 mm (25.6 in) but turns 460 mm (18.1 in), with a turning height of 400 mm (15.7 in). Tool positions are listed as 4/6/8, where the turret machines beside it have 12.

Turning height is what separates the Honor Seiki VL-46M from the other 12-position machine on its page. It is listed at 380 mm (14.9 in), where the VL-46A/AR has 450 mm (17.7 in). Everything else in the two columns is identical: 560 mm (22 in) of swing and turning diameter, a 305 mm (12 in) chuck, a 25-2,500 rpm spindle, 12 tool positions and a 450 kg (992 lb) workpiece limit.

Two spindles, two turrets and a 380 mm (14.9 in) turning height: the Honor Seiki VL-46MT is the twin version of the VL-46M . Its other rows are those of the VL-46 frame, with 560 mm (22 in) of swing and turning diameter, a 305 mm (12 in) chuck, a 25-2,500 rpm spindle range, 12+12 tool positions and a 450 kg (992 lb) workpiece limit.

An 18 in chuck and 750 mm of turning height put the Honor Seiki VL-66A/AR in the middle of the High Speed Series. The table lists a 457 mm (18 in) chuck, 800 mm (31.4 in) of swing, a 760 mm (29.9 in) turning diameter, 750 mm (29.5 in) of turning height and a spindle range of 25-2,000 rpm. The A and AR are given as one column.

The Honor Seiki VL-66AT doubles up the VL-66 frame. Each of its two spindles carries a 457 mm (18 in) chuck and runs 25-2,000 rpm, and each of its two turrets has 12 tool positions. The capacity rows read 800 mm (31.4 in) of swing, 760 mm (29.9 in) of turning diameter, 750 mm (29.5 in) of turning height and 650 kg (1,433 lb) of workpiece weight.

The Honor Seiki VL-66C opens the maker's Heavy Duty Series: a box way vertical lathe that swings and turns 850 mm (33.4 in), takes parts 650 mm (25.5 in) tall and carries 1,500 kg (3,307 lb). It is a turning-only machine. The live spindle row of the table shows a dash in the C column and a speed only for the VL-66CM beside it.
Standard Chuck: Hydraulic 3-jaw chuck & cylinder, size as spec.

Description: A live spindle running 50-2,250 rpm is what the M adds to the Honor Seiki VL-66CM. The rest of its column is shared with the turning-only VL-66C : 850 mm (33.4 in) of swing and turning diameter, 650 mm (25.5 in) of turning height, 12 tool positions and a 1,500 kg (3,307 lb) workpiece limit.
Standard Chuck: Hydraulic 3-jaw chuck & cylinder, size as spec.

Description: The Honor Seiki VL-66H is the VL-66 with the widest swing, 850 mm (33.4 in), and the shortest turning height, 620 mm (24.4 in). Its turning diameter of 760 mm (29.9 in) matches the VL-66A/AR . Where the VL-66A/AR has 12 tool positions, the table lists 4/6/8 here.

On paper the Honor Seiki VL-66M gives up envelope in two directions compared with its neighbour. Turning diameter is 700 mm (27.5 in) and turning height 650 mm (25.5 in), while the VL-66A/AR reaches 760 mm (29.9 in) and 750 mm (29.5 in). Swing is the same 800 mm (31.4 in), and so are the 457 mm (18 in) chuck, the 25-2,000 rpm spindle, the 12 tool positions and the 650 kg (1,433 lb) load limit.

The Honor Seiki VL-66MT is the M-configured twin on the VL-66 frame, with a turning diameter of 700 mm (27.5 in) and a turning height of 650 mm (25.5 in) on each of two spindles. Swing is 800 mm (31.4 in), the chucks are 457 mm (18 in), the spindle range is 25-2,000 rpm and tool positions are listed as 12+12.

The Honor Seiki VL-86A/AR is a one-metre-swing vertical lathe: 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of swing, an 860 mm (33.9 in) turning diameter and 810 mm (31.9 in) of turning height over a 533 mm (21 in) chuck. It is the largest High Speed Series model that still ships with a hydraulic 3-jaw chuck as standard, and its spindle range is 25-1,500 rpm.

The Honor Seiki VL-86AT puts two 533 mm (21 in) hydraulic chucks side by side in one machine. It is the largest Twin series model that keeps hydraulic 3-jaw chucks as standard, and each spindle is listed with 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of swing, 860 mm (33.9 in) of turning diameter, 810 mm (31.9 in) of turning height and a 25-1,500 rpm speed range. Tool positions are 12+12.

Between the 850 mm VL-66C and the 1,200 mm VL-100C , Honor Seiki places the VL-86C at 950 mm (37.4 in) of swing and turning diameter with a 2,000 kg (4,409 lb) workpiece limit. Turning height is 650 mm (25.5 in) and the table lists 12 tool positions. It is the turning-only member of its pair; the VL-86CM is the one with a live spindle.
Standard Chuck: Hydraulic 3-jaw chuck & cylinder, size as spec.

Description: The Honor Seiki VL-86CM is a 950 mm (37.4 in) vertical turning center with a 2,000 kg (4,409 lb) workpiece limit and a live spindle listed at 50-2,250 rpm. It shares the frame figures of the VL-86C , including the 650 mm (25.5 in) turning height and the 12 tool positions, and differs from it by the driven spindle alone.
Standard Chuck: Hydraulic 3-jaw chuck & cylinder, size as spec.

Description: Of the three H models in the High Speed Series, the Honor Seiki VL-86H gives away the least. Swing is 1,000 mm (39.4 in) and turning diameter 860 mm (33.9 in), both equal to the VL-86A/AR , and turning height is 800 mm (31.5 in), only slightly under that machine's 810 mm (31.9 in). The one real difference is in the tool position row, which reads 4/6/8.

With the Honor Seiki VL-86M the buyer gets the 1,000 mm (39.4 in) swing and 533 mm (21 in) chuck of the VL-86 frame, and a cutting envelope of 800 mm (31.5 in) in diameter by 700 mm (27.5 in) in height. The spindle runs 25-1,500 rpm, the tool carrier has 12 positions and the chuck may carry 850 kg (1,874 lb).

Each spindle of the Honor Seiki VL-86MT turns 800 mm (31.5 in) in diameter and 700 mm (27.5 in) in height, under a 1,000 mm (39.4 in) swing. The chucks are 533 mm (21 in), the speed range is 25-1,500 rpm and the load limit is 850 kg (1,874 lb). With two spindles and two turrets, tool positions come to 12+12.

The Honor Seiki VL-100A/AR tops the High Speed Series and behaves differently from the three sizes under it. Its chuck is listed at 1,000 mm (40 in), nearly double the 533 mm (21 in) of the VL-86A/AR , and the spindle range drops to 5-850 rpm. Swing is 1,320 mm (52 in), turning diameter 1,100 mm (43.3 in) and turning height 920 mm (36.2 in).

The Honor Seiki VL-100AT is the largest machine in the Twin series: two spindles, each with a chuck listed at 1,000 mm (40 in), a 1,320 mm (52 in) swing, a 1,100 mm (43.3 in) turning diameter and 920 mm (36.2 in) of turning height. The spindles run 5-850 rpm and tool positions are 12+12.

At 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of swing and turning diameter and 3,500 kg (7,716 lb) on the table, the Honor Seiki VL-100C is the point in the Heavy Duty Series where the hydraulic chuck gives way to a table with a manual 4-jaw chuck as standard. Turning height is 650 mm (25.5 in), and the tool carrier has 12 positions.
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: The Honor Seiki VL-100CM combines a 1,200 mm (47.2 in) turning diameter and a 3,500 kg (7,716 lb) table load with a live spindle listed at 50-2,250 rpm. It is the milling-capable version of the VL-100C and, like that machine, is named in Honor Seiki's standard list as having a fixed type crossrail. Turning height is 650 mm (25.5 in).
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: Height is the whole case for the Honor Seiki VL-100CR. It turns 800 mm (31.4 in) tall, where the VL-100C stops at 650 mm (25.5 in), and it is the only turning-only model on its page to break the 650 mm figure. Swing and turning diameter stay at 1,200 mm (47.2 in), the load limit at 3,500 kg (7,716 lb) and the tool positions at 12.
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: The Honor Seiki VL-100CRM carries both of the upgrades found on its page: the 800 mm (31.4 in) turning height of the R models and the 50-2,250 rpm live spindle of the M models. Turning diameter is 1,200 mm (47.2 in) and the workpiece limit 3,500 kg (7,716 lb), as on the other three VL-100 columns of the Heavy Duty table.
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: The Honor Seiki VL-100M is the second of two columns on the maker's VL-100 page, and in the published table it is almost a copy of the first. Swing is 1,320 mm (52 in), turning diameter 1,100 mm (43.3 in), chuck 1,000 mm (40 in), spindle range 5-850 rpm, tool positions 12 and maximum workpiece weight 1,000 kg (2,205 lb). Each of those matches the VL-100A/AR .

The Honor Seiki VL-100MT is the M-configured twin at the top of the series, and it differs from the VL-100AT only slightly, in the turning height row of the table: 900 mm (35.4 in) here against 920 mm (36.2 in) there. Swing is 1,320 mm (52 in), turning diameter 1,100 mm (43.3 in), the chucks are listed at 1,000 mm (40 in), the spindles run 5-850 rpm and tool positions are 12+12.

The Honor Seiki VL-125C is where the Heavy Duty Series changes scale. Swing and turning diameter are 1,600 mm (63.0 in), turning height is 1,200 mm (47.2 in) and the table is rated for 5,000 kg (11,023 lb). Below it, the VL-100C turns 1,200 mm (47.2 in) across but only 650 mm (25.5 in) tall, so the step to the VL-125 nearly doubles the height available.
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: Sixteen tool positions and a live spindle set the Honor Seiki VL-125CM apart from the VL-125C . The table gives it a 50-2,250 rpm live spindle, 16 positions where the C has 12, and a turning height of 1,170 mm (46.0 in). Swing and turning diameter are 1,600 mm (63.0 in) and the workpiece limit is 5,000 kg (11,023 lb).
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: Two metres of turning diameter and eight tonnes on the table define the Honor Seiki VL-160C. The table lists 2,000 mm (78.7 in) for both swing and turning diameter, 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of turning height, 12 tool positions and a maximum workpiece weight of 8,000 kg (17,637 lb).
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: Honor Seiki lists two machines that turn 2,000 mm and also mill, and the VL-160CM is the conventional one of the pair: a Heavy Duty Series vertical turning center with a live spindle at 50-2,250 rpm, 16 tool positions, 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of swing and turning diameter, 1,170 mm (46.0 in) of turning height and an 8,000 kg (17,637 lb) workpiece limit.
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: The Honor Seiki VL-200C turns 2,500 mm (98.4 in) in diameter and 1,480 mm (58.2 in) in height, and carries 12,000 kg (26,455 lb). It is also the smallest model for which Honor Seiki lists its Solid lock clamping system as standard equipment; the accessory list names the VL-200 and VL-250 for that item.
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: For twelve-tonne parts that need holes and milled faces as well as turned diameters, Honor Seiki offers the VL-200CM. Its figures are 2,500 mm (98.4 in) of swing and turning diameter, 1,480 mm (58.2 in) of turning height, a 12,000 kg (26,455 lb) workpiece limit, 16 tool positions and a live spindle running 50-2,250 rpm.
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: The Honor Seiki VL-250C is the largest turning-only model in the Heavy Duty Series, with a 3,000 mm (118.1 in) swing, a 2,970 mm (116.9 in) turning diameter, 1,480 mm (58.2 in) of turning height and a 15,000 kg (33,069 lb) workpiece limit. It is the one machine on its page where swing and turning diameter are not the same number.
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: The Honor Seiki VL-250CM is the top of the Heavy Duty Series with driven tools: a vertical turning center that swings 3,000 mm (118.1 in), turns 2,970 mm (116.9 in) across and 1,480 mm (58.2 in) tall, carries 15,000 kg (33,069 lb) and has a 50-2,250 rpm live spindle with 16 tool positions.
Standard Chuck: Table with manual 4-jaw chuck as spec.

Description: The Honor Seiki VL-300C is the first model in the maker's Large vertical lathe range. It swings and turns 3,600 mm (141.7 in), accepts parts 2,000 mm (78.7 in) tall and is rated for a 30,000 kg (66,138 lb) workpiece, with 16 tool positions.

Twenty tool positions and a 50-2,250 rpm live spindle make the Honor Seiki VL-300CM the milling-capable entry to the Large vertical lathe range. The envelope is the same as the VL-300C : 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of swing and turning diameter, 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of turning height and 30,000 kg (66,138 lb) on the table.

With a 4,500 mm (177.1 in) swing and turning diameter, the Honor Seiki VL-400C sits second in the Large vertical lathe range. It keeps the 2,000 mm (78.7 in) turning height and 16 tool positions of the VL-300C and raises the workpiece limit to 40,000 kg (88,183 lb).

The Honor Seiki VL-400CM is a 4,500 mm (177.1 in) vertical turning center for parts up to 40,000 kg (88,183 lb). Its live spindle runs 50-2,250 rpm, its tool carrier has 20 positions and its turning height is 2,000 mm (78.7 in).

Eighty tonnes is the figure that marks out the Honor Seiki VL-500C. Its table is rated for 80,000 kg (176,367 lb), double the 40,000 kg (88,183 lb) of the VL-400C below it, and the machine swings and turns 6,000 mm (236.2 in). Turning height rises as well, to 2,600 mm (102.3 in).

The Honor Seiki VL-500CM has 24 tool positions, the highest count in the VL range, alongside a 50-2,250 rpm live spindle. It turns 6,000 mm (236.2 in) in diameter and 2,600 mm (102.3 in) in height and carries 80,000 kg (176,367 lb).

The Honor Seiki VL-600C is the largest vertical lathe in the maker's published range. It swings and turns 7,000 mm (275.5 in), takes work 2,600 mm (102.3 in) tall and is rated for a 100,000 kg (220,459 lb) workpiece. Sixteen tool positions are listed, and there is no live spindle on the C model.

At the top of Honor Seiki's VL tables stands the VL-600CM: 7,000 mm (275.5 in) of swing and turning diameter, 2,600 mm (102.3 in) of turning height, a 100,000 kg (220,459 lb) workpiece limit, 24 tool positions and a live spindle listed at 50-2,250 rpm.

The Huron AX M 200 is a CNC turning centre with a 12-station live-tool turret and a tailstock. It turns up to 330 mm (13.0 in) in diameter and 625 mm in length, takes 52 mm bar through an A2-6 spindle nose, and runs the spindle to 4,500 rpm.

Power is what separates the Huron AX M 300 from the smaller AX machines. Its main spindle is rated 36 kW and 385 Nm at up to 4,000 rpm, on an A2-8 nose with a 75 mm bore and 65 mm of bar capacity. Maximum turning diameter is 420 mm (16.5 in) and turning length 600 mm.

The Huron AX MSY 200 is the full-specification version of the 200-size AX: live tools (M), a secondary spindle (S) and a Y axis (Y). With it a part can be turned and milled on one end, handed to the second spindle, and finished on the other end without leaving the machine.

The Huron AX MSY 300 is the largest and most complete AX turning centre. Its 36 kW main spindle is backed by a secondary spindle of 21.6 kW, and a 12-station live turret with ± 50 mm of Y works at both.

The Huron AX MY 200 adds a Y axis to the AX turning centre. The turret can move ± 40 mm off the spindle centreline, which turns the live tools from simple cross-drilling units into a small milling axis for pockets, flats and off-centre holes.
The Huron AX MY 300 is the large-frame AX with Y-axis milling. It joins a 36 kW, 385 Nm turning spindle to a 12-station live turret that travels ± 50 mm in Y, and it keeps a tailstock for long work.

The Huron DX 135 nvu is the smallest lathe in Huron's turning range and the fastest: a 6,000 rpm spindle on an A2-4 nose, for parts up to 220 mm (8.7 in) in diameter and 240 mm long. Bar capacity is 30 mm.

The Huron DX 170 nvu puts a 44 mm bar capacity into the smallest DX enclosure. It shares the 1,920 x 1,500 mm footprint and 120 x 240 mm travels of the DX 135 nvu , but its A2-5 spindle has a 55 mm bore and more power.

The Huron DX 200-3 is a compact two-axis CNC turning centre for short chucking parts. It turns up to 320 mm (12.6 in) in diameter and 320 mm in length, weighs 2,500 kg (5,512 lb) and fits in a space of 2,163 x 1,465 mm.

The Huron DX 200-3 B is the big-bore version of the shortest DX 200 lathe. It keeps a 300 mm (11.8 in) turning length and a 320 mm turning diameter, but its A2-6 spindle has a 70 mm bore and takes 52 mm bar.

The Huron DX 200-4 A is a 400 mm (15.7 in) turning-length lathe with the small spindle of the DX 200 series: A2-5 nose, 55 mm bore, 44 mm bar capacity. Maximum turning diameter is 320 mm over a 500 mm swing.

Combine 400 mm (15.7 in) of turning length with a 52 mm bar capacity and you get the Huron DX 200-4 B. It is a slant-bed CNC turning centre with an A2-6 spindle, a 70 mm bore and an 8-station servo turret.

The Huron DX 200-5 A marks the step to the larger DX 200 frame. Maximum turning diameter rises to 365 mm (14.4 in), cross travel to 200 mm and turning length to 500 mm, and the tailstock thrust goes up to 500 kgf.

A 75 mm bar capacity is the reason to look at the Huron DX 200-5 B. Its A2-8 spindle has a 90 mm bore, the largest in the DX 200 series, on a lathe that turns 365 mm (14.4 in) in diameter and 500 mm in length.

The Huron DX 200-5A nvu is the restyled version of the 500 mm DX 200 lathe with the A2-6 spindle. Capacity figures are those of the classic model: 365 mm (14.4 in) maximum turning diameter, 500 mm turning length, a 70 mm bore and 52 mm of bar capacity.

The Huron DX 200-5B nvu is the big-bore lathe of the nvu generation in the 200 size. Its A2-8 spindle has a 90 mm bore and takes 75 mm bar, on a machine that turns 365 mm (14.4 in) in diameter and 500 mm in length.

The Huron DX 200-7 A stretches the DX 200 platform to 700 mm (27.6 in) of turning length. With a 365 mm maximum turning diameter and an A2-6 spindle it is a medium shaft lathe on a base that weighs 4,300 kg (9,480 lb).
The Huron DX 200-7 B pairs the 700 mm (27.6 in) bed of the DX 200 series with its largest spindle. It turns 365 mm in diameter, passes 75 mm bar through a 90 mm bore, and carries an A2-8 nose.

The Huron DX 200-12 A is the long-bed shaft lathe of the DX 200 series, with 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of turning length and Z travel. Turning diameter is 365 mm, the spindle is the A2-6 unit, and the machine is 3,625 mm long.

The Huron DX 200-12 B is the top specification in the DX 200 series: the longest bed with the largest spindle. It turns parts up to 1,200 mm (47.2 in) long and 365 mm in diameter, and its A2-8 spindle passes 75 mm bar through a 90 mm bore.

The Huron DX 250-500 is a short-bed chucking lathe with a large diameter capacity for its size. It turns up to 490 mm (19.3 in) across and 500 mm long, with 250 mm of X travel, on a machine weighing 4,000 kg (8,818 lb).

The Huron DX 250-500 nvu is the largest lathe in the nvu group. It turns up to 490 mm (19.3 in) in diameter, has 250 mm of cross travel and a standard turning diameter of 300 mm, and keeps a 500 mm turning length.

The Huron DX 250-700 is a 700 mm (27.6 in) turning centre built for heavier cutting than its capacity alone suggests. It weighs 5,750 kg (12,676 lb), which is nearly half as much again as the short DX 250-500 , and turns up to 480 mm in diameter.

With a full metre between chuck and centre, the Huron DX 250-1000 is the shaft version of the DX 250. It turns 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in length and 480 mm in diameter, on a 45° slant-bed machine weighing 6,000 kg (13,228 lb).
The Huron DX 350-700 A is where the DX 350 frame begins: a 740 mm swing, a standard turning diameter of 415 mm and a maximum of 600 mm (23.6 in), with 700 mm of turning length. X travel is 310 mm.

The Huron DX 350-700 B is a heavy-duty chucker: an A2-11 spindle with a 110 mm bore, 27.8/18.5 kW on the Siemens motor, and a speed range that tops out at 1,500 rpm. It turns 600 mm (23.6 in) in diameter and 700 mm in length.

The Huron DX 350-1000 A offers a metre of turning length with a 600 mm (23.6 in) turning diameter, using the faster A2-8 spindle of the DX 350 frame. It is a general-purpose large lathe for shafts with big flanges, rolls and long hubs.

For heavy shafts a metre long, Huron offers the DX 350-1000 B. It joins a 1,000 mm (39.4 in) bed to the A2-11 spindle: 110 mm bore, 90 mm of bar capacity, and 27.8/18.5 kW on the Siemens motor at 50-1,500 rpm.

The Huron DX 350-1500 A belongs to a different weight class from the shorter DX 350 lathes. It weighs 10,000 kg (22,046 lb), turns 1,500 mm (59.1 in) in length and 600 mm in diameter, and has a tailstock rated for 1,000 kgf.

The Huron DX 350-1500 B is a 10,000 kg (22,046 lb) turning centre for long, heavy parts. It has the A2-11 spindle with a 110 mm bore, a 12-station turret and a 1,000 kgf tailstock, and it turns 1,500 mm (59.1 in) by 600 mm.

Two metres between centres is the headline of the Huron DX 350-2000 A. It turns 2,000 mm (78.7 in) in length and 600 mm in diameter, with the A2-8 spindle that runs to 2,500 rpm, and weighs 10,200 kg (22,487 lb).
The Huron DX 350-2000 B is the largest machine in the DX 250/350 series: 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of turning length, a 110 mm spindle bore and a 12-station turret. It weighs 10,200 kg (22,487 lb).

The Huron DX 500-1000 A is the entry point to the DX Large series of heavy turning centres. It turns 700 mm (27.6 in) in diameter and 1,000 mm in length on a 9,500 kg (20,944 lb) machine, and of the three spindle versions it is the one that runs fastest, at 50-2,500 rpm.

The Huron DX 500-1000 B is the middle spindle option on the 1,000 mm DX Large bed. It has an A2-11 nose, a 110 mm bore and 90 mm of bar capacity, with 26/22 kW on the Fanuc motor or 33/22 kW on the Siemens motor at 50-1,500 rpm.

A 180 mm spindle bore defines the Huron DX 500-1000 C. On an A2-15 nose, with 37/30 kW from the Fanuc motor or 45/30 kW from the Siemens motor, it is the big-bore, high-power version of the 1,000 mm DX Large lathe.

The Huron DX 500-1250 A moves the DX Large series up to an 800 mm (31.5 in) turning diameter. It has 410 mm of X travel, a standard turning diameter of 600 mm and 1,250 mm of turning length, and it weighs 10,000 kg (22,046 lb).
The Huron DX 500-1250 B is a heavy turning centre for work up to 800 mm (31.5 in) in diameter and 1,250 mm long, built around an A2-11 spindle with a 110 mm bore. It weighs 10,000 kg (22,046 lb).

The Huron DX 500-1250 C pairs the largest spindle of the DX Large series with the 800 mm (31.5 in) frame. An A2-15 nose, a 180 mm bore and 37/30 kW on the Fanuc motor, or 45/30 kW on Siemens, drive parts up to 1,250 mm long.

The Huron DX 500-2000 A is a two-metre heavy lathe with a fast spindle. It turns 2,000 mm (78.7 in) in length and 800 mm in diameter, weighs 12,500 kg (27,557 lb), and its A2-8 spindle runs 50-2,500 rpm.

The Huron DX 500-2000 B turns parts up to 2,000 mm (78.7 in) long and 800 mm in diameter with an A2-11 spindle of 110 mm bore. It is the mid-powered version of the two-metre DX Large lathe, rated 26/22 kW on Fanuc and 33/22 kW on Siemens.

The Huron DX 500-2000 C is the heaviest-duty machine on the DX 500 frame: a two-metre bed, a 180 mm spindle bore and 45/30 kW from the Siemens motor, or 37/30 kW from Fanuc. Turning capacity is 800 mm (31.5 in) by 2,000 mm.
The Huron DX 750-1250 A is a 19,500 kg (42,989 lb) turning centre for parts up to 920 mm (36.2 in) in diameter. Swing over the bed is 1,050 mm, X travel 480 mm and turning length 1,250 mm.

The Huron DX 750-1250 B puts the top spindle of the DX Large series on the DX 750 frame. It has an A2-15 nose, a 180 mm bore and 37/30 kW on Fanuc or 45/30 kW on Siemens, and it turns 920 mm (36.2 in) by 1,250 mm.
Three metres of turning length and 920 mm (36.2 in) of turning diameter make the Huron DX 750-3000 A the longest lathe in Huron's turning range. It weighs 24,000 kg (52,910 lb) and is 9,120 mm long.

The Huron DX 750-3000 B is the largest turning centre Huron lists. It combines 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of turning length, a 920 mm turning diameter and the A2-15 spindle with its 180 mm bore, in a machine of 24,000 kg (52,910 lb).

Description: The Hwacheon UPR-600B is a long-bed, low-speed lathe that turns Ø600 mm (Ø23.6 in) work up to 3,000 mm (118.1 in) between centres, with a linear-motor feed drive. Its spec table is unusual for a lathe in this size class: a minimum turning diameter of Ø180 mm (Ø7.1 in), a spindle speed of 1 ~ 300 rpm in three automatic steps, and a manual V4 tool post with 4 tool faces instead of a turret. Swing is Ø2,100 mm (Ø82.68 in). Description: The Johnford SL-20 is the smallest horizontal turning center in the SL range: a 6 in chuck, Ø42 mm (Ø1.7 in) bar capacity and a 6,000 rpm spindle on an A2-5 nose. It is the only SL model that reaches 6,000 rpm, and the only one with a 5.5 / 7.5 kW (7.4 / 10.1 hp) motor.

An 8 in chuck and an 11 / 15 kW (14.8 / 20.1 hp) spindle make the Johnford SL-30 the general-purpose size of the small SL turning centers. Bar capacity is Ø51 mm (Ø2 in), the spindle nose is A2-6 and top speed is 4,500 rpm.

The Johnford SL-35 looks like a sibling of the SL-30 on paper and is a different machine underneath. It keeps the 8 in chuck, Ø51 mm (Ø2 in) bar capacity and 11 / 15 kW (14.8 / 20.1 hp), 4,500 rpm spindle. The bed changes: a 45° slant bed replaces the 30° saddle of the SL-20 and SL-30.
Z Axis Travel: 400 mm (15.7 in); 300 mm (11.8 in) with Y-axis

Description: The Johnford SL-35-2S is the smallest twin-spindle lathe in the SL range. An 8 in main chuck faces a 6 in sub-spindle chuck across 400 mm (15.7 in) of Z travel, so a part can be turned on one side, handed over and finished on the other without leaving the machine.

The Johnford SL-40 opens the medium-sized SL series with a 10 in chuck, Ø76.5 mm (Ø3 in) bar capacity and a swing of Ø580 mm (Ø22.8 in) over the bed. At 4,000 rpm it is the fastest spindle of the medium group.
Z Axis Travel: 600 mm (23.6 in); 500 mm (19.7 in) with Y-axis
Tailstock Travel: 500 mm (19.7 in); 400 mm (15.7 in) with Y-axis

Description: Shaft work is what the L adds. The Johnford SL-40L stretches the SL-40 to 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of Z travel and 900 mm (35.4 in) of tailstock travel, on the same 10 in chuck and 4,000 rpm, 11 / 15 kW (14.8 / 20.1 hp) spindle.
Z Axis Travel: 1,000 mm (39.4 in); 900 mm (35.4 in) with Y-axis
Tailstock Travel: 900 mm (35.4 in); 800 mm (31.5 in) with Y-axis

Description: The Johnford SL-50 is where the SL range gets its heavy construction: a 45° bed, a 2 step automatic spindle transmission and a programmable hydraulic tailstock as standard. Chuck size is 10 in and bar capacity Ø76.5 mm (Ø3 in), the same as on the lighter SL-40 .
Z Axis Travel: 650 mm (25.6 in); 550 mm (21.7 in) with Y-axis
Tailstock Travel: 530 mm (20.9 in); 430 mm (16.9 in) with Y-axis

Description: On the Johnford SL-50-2S a sub-spindle with an 8 in chuck takes the place of the tailstock, opposite a 10 in main chuck. Z travel is 500 mm (19.7 in) and the bed swings Ø580 mm (Ø22.8 in).
Swing Over Cross Slide: Ø450 mm (Ø17.7 in) / Ø380 mm (Ø15 in) (Y-axis)

Description: Take the short SL-50 bed and fit the larger A spindle, and the result is the Johnford SL-50A: a 12 in chuck, a Ø115 mm (Ø4.5 in) spindle bore and 22 / 26 kW (29.5 / 34.9 hp) on a machine with 650 mm (25.6 in) of Z travel.
Bar Capacity: Ø91 mm (Ø3.6 in) / Ø102 mm (Ø4 in) (Opt.)
Z Axis Travel: 650 mm (25.6 in); 550 mm (21.7 in) with Y-axis
Tailstock Travel: 530 mm (20.9 in); 430 mm (16.9 in) with Y-axis

Description: A 12 in, 22 / 26 kW (29.5 / 34.9 hp) main spindle and an 8 in sub-spindle, 500 mm (19.7 in) apart at most: the Johnford SL-50A-2S is the heavy short twin-spindle lathe of the SL range.
Swing Over Cross Slide: Ø450 mm (Ø17.7 in) / Ø380 mm (Ø15 in) (Y-axis)
Bar Capacity: Ø91 mm (Ø3.6 in) / Ø102 mm (Ø4 in) (Opt.)

Description: The KAAST A-Turn 300/700 is a CNC turning center with a 500 mm (19.7 in) maximum turning diameter, a 700 mm (27.6 in) maximum turning length, a 12-station turret and a tailstock with an MT5 quill. In base form it is an X and Z machine under the FANUC 0i-T control. A C axis and live tooling are both listed as options.

The KAAST A-Turn SYM 300 Y is a turning center with a Y axis and live tooling: ±50 mm (±1.9 in) of Y travel, a 12-station turret and driven tools listed with 4.5 kW (6 hp) and 6,000 rpm. Maximum turning diameter is 420 mm (16.5 in) and maximum turning length 540 mm (21 in), under the FANUC 0i-TF control.
Sub Spindle: No (sub-spindle on the 300 S and 300 SY versions)

Description: The KAAST F-Turn 330/820 is a heavy CNC lathe for large-bore work: 820 mm (32.28 in) between centers, a maximum turning diameter of Ø500 mm (19.5 in) and a spindle bore of Ø102 mm (3.95 in), or Ø165 mm (6.5 in) as an option. It weighs 8,870 kg (19,514 lb) and runs under the Fanuc 0i-TF control.
Spindle Bore: Ø102 mm (3.95 in) (opt. Ø165 mm / 6.5 in)
Bar Capacity: Ø89 mm (3.4 in) (opt. Ø116 mm / 4.5 in)

Description: The KAAST U-Turn 265/400 is a small, high-speed CNC lathe: a 6 in chuck on an A2-5 nose, a 6,000 rpm spindle and a 2,300 kg (5,060 lb) machine on a 2,240 x 1,700 mm (88 x 67 in) footprint. Maximum turning diameter is 370 mm (14.5 in) and maximum turning length 400 mm (15.74 in).

The KAAST V-Turn 550 appears on KAAST's vertical lathe page, and its figures describe a chucker for short, wide parts: a maximum turning diameter of Ø550 mm (21.7 in), a maximum turning height of 550 mm (21.7 in) and a maximum swing of Ø750 mm (29.5 in). It runs under the FANUC 0i-TF control.

The Kent CNC CRL-1640 is a lathe that runs in both manual and CNC modes, with a 16 in (406 mm) swing over the bed, 35 in (889 mm) between centers and a 7.5 hp (5.6 kW) spindle that reaches 3,000 rpm. The standard control is the FANUC 0i-Mate TF, with the Fagor 8055i listed as an option.
7.5 hp (5.6 kW) frequency drive; opt. 7.5 hp (5.6 kW) Fagor servo
Spindle Motor Power: 7.5 hp (5.6 kW) frequency drive; opt. 7.5 hp (5.6 kW) Fagor servo

Description: The Kent CNC CT-1118 is a small collet lathe: 11 in (279 mm) of swing over the bed, 18 in (457 mm) between centers, a 5C spindle that runs from 25 to 4,000 rpm and a guaranteed circular accuracy of 50 millionths of an inch (1.3 µm). It weighs 2,200 lb (998 kg) and stands in an 81 x 40 x 65 in (2,057 x 1,016 x 1,651 mm) footprint.
Circular Accuracy: 50 millionths of an inch (1.3 µm), guaranteed
Workholding: Step chucks up to 6 in (152 mm) diameter; lever or air-operated power collet closer

Description: The Kent CNC KLS-1840N is a fully covered CNC lathe with an 18 in (457 mm) swing over the bed, 39.4 in (1,001 mm) between centers and a 3 in (76 mm) spindle bore. It is supplied with a 10 in (254 mm) 3-jaw manual chuck, a 4-way electric tool post and the FANUC 0i-Mate TF control.
Servo Motors: FANUC servo motor for X and Z axis

Description: The KRC Velocity VTC-12 is the entry size of KRC's Velocity series of vertical turning lathes, with a 1,250 mm (49.2 in) table, a 1,500 mm (59.1 in) maximum turning diameter and 1,250 mm (49.2 in) of turning height. The table carries 6,000 kg (13,228 lb) and turns at 1 - 300 rpm.
X Axis Travel: -200 mm (-7.87 in) to 950 mm (37.4 in) (cross travel)

Description: KRC's Velocity VTC-16 is a vertical turning lathe with a 1,600 mm (63 in) table that swings 2,000 mm (78.7 in) and turns up to 1,900 mm (74.8 in) in diameter. It sits between the Velocity VTC-12 and the Velocity VTC-20 and shares its 1,600 mm (63 in) maximum turning height with the larger machine.
X Axis Travel: -250 mm (-9.84 in) to 1,125 mm (44.29 in) (cross travel)

Description: The KRC Velocity VTC-20 is the largest lathe in the Velocity series: a 2,000 mm (78.7 in) table, 2,400 mm (94.5 in) maximum turning diameter, 2,500 mm (98.4 in) swing and a table load of 13,000 kg (28,660 lb).
X Axis Travel: -250 mm (-9.84 in) to 1,380 mm (54.33 in) (cross travel)

LICO files it under its turning centers, but the envelope is that of a second-operation and short-part lathe. Maximum turning length is 100 mm (4 in).

Description: The Litz LT-350 is a compact two-axis CNC turning lathe with an A2-5 spindle nose, 45 mm (1.8 in) bar capacity and a maximum turning diameter of 240 mm (9.4 in). Maximum turning length is 350 mm (13.8 in), and the spindle runs from 40-6,000 rpm.

The Litz LT-400 is a two-axis CNC turning lathe one size above the LT-350 , with an A2-6 spindle nose, 52 mm (2.0 in) bar capacity, a 320 mm (12.6 in) maximum turning diameter and 530 mm (20.9 in) of turning length.

The Litz LT-400M is an 8 in (203 mm) chuck turning centre with a C axis and a 12-station live turret, so cross holes, flats and keyways are cut in the same clamping as the turning. Turning capacity is 215 mm (8.5 in) in diameter and 530 mm (20.9 in) in length, with 52 mm (2.0 in) bar capacity.

The Litz LT-520 is the largest of the three two-axis LT slant-bed lathes: a 10 in (254 mm) chuck machine with an A2-8 spindle nose, 78 mm (3.1 in) bar capacity, a 400 mm (15.7 in) maximum turning diameter and 710 mm (28.0 in) of turning length.
The Litz LT-520M puts a C axis and a 12-station live turret on the larger LT bed: a 10 in (254 mm) chuck, an A2-8 spindle with 78 mm (3.1 in) bar capacity and 710 mm (28.0 in) of turning length.

The Milltronics SL8-II is a CNC turning center fitted with an 8 in 3-jaw hydraulic chuck on an A2-6 spindle nose, turning parts up to 14 in (356 mm) in diameter and 21 in (533 mm) long. The spindle runs up to 4,000 rpm with 30/20 hp (22.4/14.9 kW) and 161 lb-ft (218 Nm) of torque.

Description: The Milltronics SL10-II is a 10 in chuck turning center built on an A2-8 spindle nose, with 260 lb-ft (352 Nm) of spindle torque and a turning envelope of 17.7 in (450 mm) in diameter by 29.9 in (759 mm) in length. It trades speed for torque: the spindle tops out at 3,000 rpm.

The figures describe a machine for long, heavy turning at an unhurried pace: rapids are 500 ipm (12.7 m/min) and the spindle range is 40 to 2,500 rpm.

The Pinnacle L210A is a slant bed CNC turning center with an 8 in chuck, 610 mm (24.0 in) between centers and a maximum turning diameter of Ø440 mm (Ø17.3 in). It is the base model of four L210 variants that share one bed and differ in chuck and spindle.
Machine Dimensions: 2.7 x 1.6 x 1.8 m (L x W x H)

Description: Pinnacle sells a 10 in chuck in two ways, and the Pinnacle L210B is the lighter of them: the larger chuck on the A2-6 spindle of the L210A , keeping 45 - 4,500 rpm and the 11 / 15 kW (14.8 / 20.1 hp) motor.
Machine Dimensions: 2.7 x 1.6 x 1.8 m (L x W x H)

Description: Bar capacity is the reason to choose the Pinnacle L210C: Ø77 mm (Ø3.0 in), through an Ø88 mm (Ø3.5 in) spindle bore on an A2-8 nose. The L210A and L210B stop at Ø65 mm (Ø2.6 in).
Machine Dimensions: 2.7 x 1.6 x 1.8 m (L x W x H)

Description: The Pinnacle L210D carries the largest chuck in the L210 range, 12 in, on the A2-8 spindle with a 15 / 18.5 kW (20.1 / 24.8 hp) motor. It is the heaviest of the four at 4,300 kg (9,480 lb).
Machine Dimensions: 2.7 x 1.6 x 1.8 m (L x W x H)

Description: The Pinnacle PK-L150A is a compact CNC turning center for small chucked and bar-fed parts: a 6 in chuck on an A2-5 spindle, Ø42 mm (Ø1.7 in) of bar capacity and a turning length of 150 mm (5.9 in). It weighs 2,100 kg (4,630 lb) and occupies 1.8 x 1.4 x 1.65 m.

Description: The Pinnacle PK-L210A/BMY is a slant bed turning center with a VDI 30 live tooling turret and a Y axis of 80 mm (3.1 in), listed as ±40 mm. It mills, drills and taps on a turned part in the same chucking, using a C axis that positions to 0.001 degree.

Description: The ROMI VT 1400M is the smallest of Romi's ram-type vertical CNC lathes, and still a large machine: a 1,400 mm (55 in) chuck, 1,600 mm (63 in) of turning diameter and a table that accepts 10,000 kg (22,000 lbs). The M in the name refers to the driven tool in the ram, which with the C axis turns the lathe into a machine that also drills and mills.

Wide, flat work is the territory of the ROMI VT 2000M. This vertical CNC lathe turns up to 2,200 mm (87 in) in diameter on a 2,000 mm (79 in) chuck, yet its maximum turning height is the same 1,500 mm (59 in) as on the smaller VT 1400M . Slewing rings, large flanges, gear rims and tyre moulds have that shape.

From the ROMI VT 2500M upward the VT Series becomes a twin-column machine. The cross rail hangs between two cast columns joined by a traverse and is moved by two servomotors and ball screws to programmed stops, and that structure buys height: 2,100 mm (83 in) of turning height with the ram, where the two smaller models stop at 1,500 mm.

Diameter without added weight capacity: the ROMI VT 3000M turns up to 3,400 mm (134 in) on a 3,000 mm (118 in) chuck, but its table is rated for the same 25,000 kg (55,100 lbs) as the VT 2500M . It is the choice for parts that are very wide and comparatively light for their size.

The ROMI VT 5000 belongs to a different order of size from the M models below it. Its table accepts 90,000 kg (198,400 lbs), its chuck is 5,000 mm (197 in) across, and it turns parts up to 7,000 mm (276 in) in diameter and 4,000 mm (157 in) high. The machine itself weighs 207,000 kg (456,400 lbs).

Romi prints its figures in a shared column with the VTL 500ML.

Description: The ROMI VTL 500R is a vertical turning center for chucked parts up to 500 mm (20 in) in diameter, with the spindle pointing up and a 12-station turret for fixed tools above it. Romi lists it in one column with the VTL 500L and gives the two identical figures. On a vertical lathe gravity seats the part in the chuck, which is why this layout is chosen for discs, hubs, flywheels and brake components that are awkward to load horizontally.
Floor Space: 1.7 x 2.3 m (67 x 91 in) without chip conveyor

The Sharp 1840TC-F is a flat bed CNC lathe of toolroom size: 18 in (457.2 mm) of swing over the bed, 39.4 in between centers and a 2.37 in spindle bore behind a D1-6 camlock nose. It is the smallest of Sharp's TC-F lathes.

A 20 in (508 mm) swing and 59.05 in between centers define the Sharp 2060TC-F, the middle of the three smaller flat bed CNC lathes Sharp builds around the FANUC Oi-TF control. Its spindle bore is 3.37 in (85.59 mm), a full inch more than the 2.37 in (60.19 mm) of the 1840TC-F .
The Sharp 2460TC-F is the 24 in (609.6 mm) swing flat bed CNC lathe in the TC-F line, with 59 in between centers, a 4.09 in (103.88 mm) spindle bore and a Fanuc 15 hp (11.18 kW) spindle motor.

The Sharp 3060TC-F opens the 3000 series of flat bed CNC lathes: 29.92 in (760 mm) of swing over the bed, 59 in (1,500 mm) between centers and a 6.7 in (170 mm) bore through an A2-11 spindle. This is oil-country and heavy-shaft territory, a clear step above the 2460TC-F .
Turret: Hydraulic 8 position turret LS 200 with 4 X internal tool holder and 4 X external tool wedges

Description: Sharp's 3080TC-F stretches the 30 in flat bed CNC lathe to 78.75 in (2,000 mm) between centers. The headstock is the one used across the 3000 series, with a 6.7 in (170 mm) bore, an A2-11 nose and a 20 hp (14.91 kW) motor, so the choice between this model and its siblings comes down to how long the work is and how much floor can be given up.

Description: The TOS Kuřim SKD-D is a large vertical lathe with a movable cross-rail, built around a clamping plate of 4,000/5,000 mm (157.5/196.9 in) and a maximum machining diameter of 6,000 mm (236.2 in). It takes workpieces of 100,000 kg (220,459 lb).

Hydrostatic guideways on every listed axis and workpieces of 80,000 - 320,000 kg (176,367 - 705,467 lb): the TOS Kuřim SKD-E is the heavy class of the SKD vertical lathes. Clamping plates are 5,000/6,300/8,000 mm (196.9/248.0/315.0 in) and the maximum machining diameter is 6,500 - 10,000 mm (255.9 - 393.7 in).

The TOS Kuřim SKDY-D is a vertical lathe with a Y axis. Its gantry moves, giving Y travel of 3,000/5,000 mm (118.1/196.9 in) in addition to the X, Z and W motions of a conventional vertical lathe. Clamping plates are 3,000/4,000/5,000 mm (118.1/157.5/196.9 in).

The TOS Kuřim SKDY-E joins the two largest things in the catalogue: a vertical lathe for workpieces of 80,000 - 320,000 kg (176,367 - 705,467 lb) and a moving gantry with 4,500 - 6,500 mm (177.2 - 255.9 in) of Y travel above it.

The TOS Kuřim SKJ 50 is a movable-column vertical lathe that machines diameters up to 10,000 mm (393.7 in) on a clamping plate of only 5,000 mm (196.9 in). The ratio is the point of the SKJ design. The machining diameter is twice the plate.

At 150,000 kg (330,688 lb) of workpiece weight on a 6,300 mm (248.0 in) clamping plate, the TOS Kuřim SKJ 63 is the middle size of the movable-column SKJ vertical lathes. Its maximum machining diameter is 10,000 mm (393.7 in).

The TOS Kuřim SKJ 80 turns the largest parts in the maker's catalogue: a maximum machining diameter of 16,000 mm (629.9 in) and a workpiece weight of 320,000 kg (705,467 lb). Both match the series headline claims of workpiece diameter up to 16 m and tables for loads up to 320 tons.
